name: st_reference_check
description: The candidate re-judged against an automatic time-varying ST reference built like that of Smrdel & Jager (2002), who approximated the Long-Term ST Database annotators' reference. The database annotators measured ST deviations from an ST reference function joined from local references placed in non-ischaemic stretches (K22); candidates here are detected against a record-wide median instead. Same numbers as annotator_reference, plus how the change was absorbed. Per involved lead: peak_deviation_uv signed towards the candidate (positive = same direction) against the record-wide median and after each step (after_slow_trend: 30-min mean, or 4-h mean where the two differ by more than 50 uV; after_steps: inside such stretches that contain an ST-level step of the lead or a QRS-shape step, the reference follows the ST level; annotator_like_reference: deviations opposite to the lead's orientation, or under 25 uV in a lead of no orientation, absorbed); episode_at_100_uv and episode_at_150_uv (the LTSTDB episode rule re-applied against the final reference: start beyond 50 uV, at least 30 s at or beyond the threshold, overlapping the candidate); absorbed_by (the first step that takes the peak below 100 uV); steps_behind_reference_following (the QRS-shape and ST-level steps that made the reference follow the ST level, near_candidate when the step's transition lies within 144 s of the candidate); qrs_shape_step_near_candidate; orientation (E, D or U, from this lead's deviations outside the candidate) and candidate_against_lead_orientation. How to read it, in both directions: (1) episode_at_150_uv true in an involved lead: the change still stands out against a reference that follows slow trends, steps and the lead's usual direction, which counts for a genuine transient ST episode (it does not by itself separate ischemic from heart-rate related change). (2) episode_at_100_uv true and episode_at_150_uv false: the uncertain zone (Smrdel & Jager needed 150 uV with their automatic reference to match the database annotations); counts in neither direction. (3) Not an episode at 100 uV in any involved lead: read absorbed_by. orientation: the change goes against the direction this lead deviates in throughout the rest of the record, and a reference that keeps to the lead's usual direction swallows it whatever the threshold; this counts clearly against a new ischemic episode in that lead. slow_trend: the 30-min mean follows the change, as with a drift or a shifted level of the lead; counts against, but a long real episode with gradual onset and offset also pulls the 30-min mean along, so look at the ST trend before trusting it. step_with_qrs_shape_step_near_candidate: a QRS-shape step at the time of the change, as with a body-position, axis or conduction change (the database classes in the reference knowledge); counts against ischemia, the more so when the ST change starts and stops abruptly with little heart-rate change (K14) and the QRS change is in the same lead (compare_morphology). step_without_qrs_shape_step_near_candidate: the reference followed the ST level only because the change is long (the 30-min mean departs from the 4-h mean) and contains an ST-level step; a long genuine episode with a fairly quick onset and a plateau is itself detected as such a step, so this absorption counts in neither direction: judge the change by the other evidence. Evidence to weigh with the rest, not a verdict. A measurement packet, not a diagnosis.
